title: Ronaldo vs Yamal. Portugal vs Spain. The Biggest World Cup Knockout Clash Lands in Dallas on Monday.
excerpt: The Iberian rivals meet at AT&T Stadium for only the third time in World Cup history. Spain are unbeaten in 34 matches. Ronaldo has four goals and has scored in six World Cups. DFW's 300,000-strong Indian American community has a front-row seat.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Portugal faces Spain in a historic World Cup knockout clash at AT&T Stadium.
  • Spain is unbeaten in 34 matches, including four World Cup games without conceding.
  • Cristiano Ronaldo has scored four goals in this World Cup, including his first knockout goal.
  • Lamine Yamal, at 18, is Spain's key attacking player, scoring his first World Cup goal.
  • The Dallas area hosts over 300,000 Indian Americans, eager for this major sporting event.
The 2026 World Cup has produced no shortage of drama. But nothing on the remaining schedule carries the weight of what AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas, will host on Monday afternoon. Portugal vs Spain. Cristiano Ronaldo vs Lamine Yamal. A 41-year-old who has scored in six World Cups against an 18-year-old who was born the same year Ronaldo scored his first tournament goal. Kickoff is at 3 PM ET (12 PM PT) on Monday, July 6. ## How They Got Here Spain arrived with an emphatic 3-0 dismantling of Austria at SoFi Stadium on Thursday. Mikel Oyarzabal scored twice, Pedro Porro added a header, and Spain extended their unbeaten run to a staggering 34 matches — a streak that includes the Euro 2024 title and the 2025 Nations League crown. They have not conceded a single goal in four matches at this World Cup. Luis de la Fuente's side plays with the controlled fury of a team that knows it is the best in the world and feels no need to pretend otherwise. "We came close to perfection, but there is always room for improvement," de la Fuente said after the Austria rout. In coach-speak, that is a warning: Spain are not satisfied with dominance. They want history. Portugal's path was messier — and far more thrilling. Croatia took the game to the wire in Toronto before Gonçalo Ramos rescued Portugal with a 94th-minute header to secure a 2-1 win. Ronaldo opened his knockout-stage account with a penalty — remarkably, his first ever World Cup knockout goal — and Croatia's last-gasp equalizer was ruled offside by VAR. Luka Modrić, 40, walked off what may have been his final World Cup pitch. Ronaldo, 41, walked toward his next challenge. ![World Cup — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/fb/Kitzbuehel_slalom_ganslernhang_2010.jpg) > **""We came close to perfection, but there is always room for improvement," de la Fuente said after the Austria rout."** ## The Ronaldo Question Four goals in three group matches. His first knockout goal in his fifth World Cup. A record 19 career World Cup goals. Ronaldo is 41 years old and playing with a clarity that borders on defiance. His sister has called this his "last dance." Roberto Martínez, Portugal's manager, has built the team to give Ronaldo space to operate as the focal point of every attack. But Monday is different. Spain will not offer space. They will suffocate the flanks, press high through midfield, and trust that the defensive structure which has conceded zero goals in four matches can contain a player who has spent more than two decades refusing to be contained. ## The Yamal Factor On the other side of the generational divide stands Lamine Yamal. The Barcelona winger turned 18 during this tournament and has been Spain's most dangerous attacking weapon since the group stage, scoring his first World Cup goal in a 4-0 rout of Saudi Arabia. His pace, his dribbling, his willingness to take on defenders — it is all there, at an age when most footballers are still playing U-19 tournaments. The last time Ronaldo and Yamal shared a pitch was the 2025 Nations League final. Spain won on penalties. Yamal was quiet. Ronaldo scored. Both know the stakes are different this time. There is no group stage safety net. Lose, and you go home. ## Why Dallas Matters for the Diaspora ![World Cups — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/fb/Kitzbuehel_slalom_ganslernhang_2010.jpg)

The Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex is home to one of the largest Indian American communities in the United States — an estimated 300,000-plus, concentrated in Plano, Frisco, Irving, and the mid-cities corridor that surrounds AT&T Stadium in Arlington. Football's popularity among the Indian diaspora has grown enormously, fueled by Premier League and La Liga viewership. Ronaldo, in particular, enjoys massive popularity in India and among NRIs globally — his social media following includes tens of millions of Indian fans, and his brand transcends sport in a way that few athletes can match. For the hundreds of thousands of Indian Americans living within driving distance of Arlington, this is the biggest sporting event to land in their backyard since the World Cup arrived in North America. Tickets start at approximately $2,400 for upper-level seats, with lower-level seats exceeding $3,400. Whether in the stadium or watching from the restaurants and living rooms of Irving, Richardson, and Frisco, the diaspora will be watching. ## What Happens Next The winner advances to a quarterfinal against Belgium or the United States at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles on July 10 — another match with deep diaspora relevance, given LA's massive South Asian community.

This is only the third time Portugal and Spain have met at a World Cup. Spain won 1-0 in the 2010 round of 16 in South Africa. They drew 3-3 in the 2018 group stage in Russia — the match where Ronaldo announced himself with a hat trick, including an 88th-minute free kick that still ranks among the greatest World Cup goals ever scored. Monday in Dallas carries all of that history. And for the hundreds of thousands of Indian Americans who call DFW home, it carries something more: a world-class World Cup knockout match, right at their doorstep.
